items.title: Fujifilm pours $64 million into magnetic tape production as AI storage demand surges
items.content:
Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.

TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust .

Thanks, AI: Despite their origins in the early days of computing and digital media, magnetic tapes have never completely disappeared from the market. In fact, demand for data storage is so high right now that tape manufacturers are investing millions to expand their production capacity.

Fujifilm recently announced a significant new investment in its magnetic tape manufacturing operations. The Japanese giant will spend 10 billion yen, or around $64 million, to expand production capacity at its Kanagawa Factory in the city of Odawara. The site manufactures magnetic tapes for data storage workloads, and the IT world is certainly in desperate need of cheap, reliable storage these days.

The new investment will run from fiscal year 2026 through 2028, Fujifilm said . The company will use the newly allocated funds to expand Kanagawa's manufacturing facilities, with new positions expected to open as well. Fujifilm explained that magnetic tape is increasingly being used by cloud providers and data center operators, which is why the company needs to increase its manufacturing output to around five times its current level to better meet market demand.

Needless to say, Fujifilm is citing generative AI and other AI-related services as major drivers behind the growing demand for magnetic tape. The massive amounts of digital data collected by AI companies – for both model training and inference workloads – need a safe place to be stored. Magnetic tapes can hold enormous amounts of data and preserve it for long periods without requiring the significant financial investment associated with SSDs and other modern storage solutions.

Fujifilm's Kanagawa plant will focus on manufacturing the company's version of LTO-10 tapes, based on the LTO Ultrium standard. The LTO format was designed in the 1990s as an open-standard alternative to proprietary tape formats and is managed by a consortium of IT companies, including HPE, IBM, and Quantum Corporation.

LTO-10 tapes were released earlier this year, providing a native capacity of 40 terabytes. With compression, a single LTO-10 tape can store up to 100 TB . The transfer rate is 400 megabytes per second in either case, which shouldn't be an issue considering the "cold" storage workloads for which magnetic tapes are typically used.

SK Hynix expects memory chip shortage to persist until at least 2030

Furthermore, the LTO consortium is already planning the next upgrades to its tape technology. The LTO-11 format is expected to arrive in 2029, offering a native capacity of 70 TB. Future plans include tapes capable of storing 120 TB (LTO-12), 210 TB (LTO-13), and even 365 TB (LTO-14) of uncompressed data on a single cartridge. That's frankly an outrageous amount of storage, no matter how you look at it.

Fujifilm also highlighted the company's long history with magnetic tape products. Its initial research efforts began in the 1950s and continued to evolve in response to new formats, including broadcast and consumer videotape systems. Fujifilm launched its first LTO-based product, the LTO Ultrium 1, in 2000, while the latest LTO Ultrium 10 format was introduced just a year ago.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-118598 📢 Source: fedora 💣 CVSS Score: 6.5 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True A logic error in Epiphany's site permission handling can cause camera and microphone access to be granted when the user only approves a different permission. In src/ephy-window.c, set_permission() stores the user's Allow/Deny choice after a WebKit permission dialog. Types CLIPBOARD and WEBSITE_DATA_ACCESS are not stored by ephy_permission_is_stored_by_permissions_manager(), so control fell into an else-if that was written as: } else if (EPHY_PERMISSION_TYPE_ACCESS_WEBCAM_AND_MICROPHONE) { Because that expression is a non-zero enum constant, the branch always ran for those types and wrote EPHY_PERMISSION_PERMIT for both ACCESS_WEBCAM and ACCESS_MICROPHONE for the site origin. The user only saw a Clipboard or Website Data Access dialog. A malicious site that obtains approval for clipboard or third-party storage access can afterwards use getUserMedia without a further camera/microphone prompt, exposing audiovisual confidentiality. Requirements: the victim must visit a malicious page and click Allow on a clipboard or website-data-access prompt. Affected: Epiphany >= 45.0 (bug present at least through 51.x). Fixed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/epiphany/-/merge_requests/2249 (commit 480c3648). items.summary_ko: Epiphany의 사이트 권한 처리 논리 오류로, 사용자가 클립보드나 웹사이트 데이터 접근 권한만 허용해도 카메라와 마이크 권한이 함께 부여될 수 있다. 조건문이 잘못 작성되어 해당 권한 유형에서 항상 참이 되고, 카메라와 마이크 권한이 사이트 단위로 허용(PERMIT) 저장된다. 악성 사이트가 클립보드나 서드파티 저장소 권한을 얻으면 이후 추가 확인 없이 getUserMedia로 카메라와 마이크에 접근할 수 있다. 원격 악용 가능으로 표기되었으며, 영향 버전은 Epiphany 45.0 이상이다.
items.content_ko: 피해자는 악성 페이지를 방문하고 클립보드 또는 웹사이트 데이터 접근 요청에서 ‘허용’을 눌러야 한다. 원인은 ephy-window.c의 set_permission() 함수에서 저장 여부를 판단하는 else-if 조건이 enum 상수를 비교하지 않고 그대로 쓰여 있는 데 있다. 사용자는 클립보드 권한만 본다. 본문이 잘려 있어 영향을 받는 버전 범위의 나머지 설명은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Conserves Power, Resolves Brief Communications Pause
items.content:
This image, taken on April 27, 1977, shows one of the Voyagers in the 25-Foot Space Simulator thermal vacuum chamber at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

The agency’s longest-running mission is approaching a historic distance milestone as its team members implement creative engineering solutions to keep it going.

NASA’s Voyager team is celebrating two recent developments with the Voyager 1 spacecraft: In September, they successfully completed a months-long effort to stretch the spacecraft’s diminishing power supply. Then, on Oct. 20, an unexpected loss of communication with the spacecraft resolved itself after 48 hours, before the team sent commands to the spacecraft to troubleshoot the issue.

In early September, engineers successfully turned off three devices on the Voyager 1 spacecraft and substituted them with three lower-power alternatives. Nicknamed the “Big Bang,” the energy-saving effort was completed about six weeks after the mission team performed the same swap on Voyager 2. The Big Bang will enable Voyager 1’s remaining science instruments to operate longer than previously anticipated.

The Voyagers get their power from radioisotope thermoelectric generators , which convert heat from decaying plutonium into electricity. With the plutonium supply continually depleting, both probes lose about 4 watts of power each year. Almost a half-century since Voyager launched, the spacecraft power margins have grown thin, requiring the team to conserve energy by shutting off nonessential devices and systems.

The Big Bang was unique because it required the swaps to occur simultaneously. The six devices help keep the spacecraft warm enough to operate in the frigid expanse of space, and only by swapping all three could the team both reduce the amount of power Voyager 1 uses and ensure that heat is properly distributed on the spacecraft.

In recent years, the dwindling power supply has forced the team to turn off two science instruments . The mission launched in 1977 with 10 dedicated science instruments, some of which were turned off after the spacecraft’s planetary encounters. Some instruments were left on to study the outer region of the heliosphere , a bubble of particles and magnetic fields created by the Sun. Now, the Voyagers are traveling through interstellar space, the area outside the heliosphere, and are the only spacecraft to ever study this region directly. Without performing the Big Bang, the mission would have needed to turn off another instrument on Voyager 1 as early as summer 2027.

But between now and summer 2027, the team is at the ready for more surprises like the one they recently encountered when they briefly lost contact with Voyager 1 on Oct. 18 and 19. NASA’s Deep Space Network — large antennas at three facilities around the globe used to communicate with spacecraft at the Moon and beyond — was unable to detect a radio signal from the probe, which is 16 billion miles (24 billion kilometers) from Earth, during two scheduled communications attempts, 24 hours apart. The spacecraft’s signal reappeared 24 hours later, on Oct. 20, and the team has maintained communication with it since then.

Engineers still are investigating what caused the communication loss. The team has so far determined that one group of thrusters went offline and their backups turned on. Such a swap is programmed to occur automatically if the spacecraft computers detect something amiss with the active thrusters. This automatic response is known as fault protection and directs the spacecraft to put itself in a safe, or stable, configuration and pause normal operations, giving engineers time to diagnose the issue and take action.

items.title: Why VPNs Are Worth Defending
items.content:
Developers of virtual private network (VPN) apps are reporting that their products are again being pulled from Apple’s App Store in Russia. This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Why? VPNs give people a way to control their own online activities. When you visit a website through a VPN, that website only sees the VPN server's location (well, IP address) rather than your actual location. It's like sending a letter through a P.O. box so the recipient doesn't know where you really live. It can also disguise where you’re accessing information from, which can make it possible to access information banned by your government.

This is an unacceptable crackdown on a vital tool to protect privacy and speech online.

Going after tools that give people the space to communicate and access information freely is a common tactic from the totalitarian playbook. This latest demand comes after several steps the Russian government’s taken to surveil speech specifically on Apple products. In 2024, the Moscow Times reported that Russia’s state media watchdog, Roskomnadzor, went after VPN apps on the Apple App Store, after banning access to Western social media platforms and blacklisting opposition media sites. Russia then blocked Apple’s FaceTime software in 2025, according to Apple Insider.

Bloomberg also recently reported that the Russian government has added Apple and Microsoft to its state surveillance registry. This gives Roskomnadzor access to local users’ correspondence, Apple Insider reported , and puts both companies in a position to turn over customer information to the country’s security services as required.

With government control encroaching on their devices and less access to tools that give them alternate methods, people in Russia are left with shrinking options to communicate online or find information that isn’t state-sanctioned.

While Russia’s actions offer a more extreme vision of what happens when the government tries to enforce speech rules by attacking vital privacy tools, it is far from the only government doing so. Several states in the U.S., bent on making it difficult to circumvent invasive age-gating laws, have suggested banning VPNs—either to access certain content or in some cases to simply ban them outright. EFF has publicly (and loudly) criticized these proposals, because going after VPNs is a dangerous step down the road of censorship.

Attacks on speech and privacy online are deeply troubling, no matter where they happen. What those in power may see as a “loophole” in their invasive laws is actually an expression of user control. We’ll continue to speak out when we see governments going after them to take that control away.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Florilegium: Procedural Flowers in LaTeX
items.content:
asked how to make flowers like these in LaTeX. I don't know how the original was made, and

this project doesn't try to reproduce it. It is one possible way, and the way I did it:

hand-authored primitives with randomized parameters, painted in Lua, placed by a procedural

layout whose "fill the unused space" part borrows a 1998 idea from the ornament literature.

Procedurally generated Delft-blue floral page margins for LaTeX. No images, no imported

paths, no external assets: every petal, leaf and stem is a parametric curve computed in Lua

while the page is being written, painted like a watercolor, and written straight into the

Six seeds of the grown composition. Same code, different seed — and the garden fills

Two documents share one package, and a third shows what else it does:

authored : stems, leaves and flowers placed by hand, every parameter sampled

grown : a plant grown to fit the page by a greedy space-filling loop

the page layout, and the free space below the text on the last page

Both PDFs are self-describing: the body text is the write-up of how the margin is drawn.

Last page of the grown document: the text ends early, so branches arch into the space below.

300 dpi crop. Mottled washes with white streaks lifted out, lobed leaves with white veins,

forget-me-not cymes, a pale ghost flower behind the stems.

Seed 6, from an empty margin to the finished page. The stems rise first, leaves open as

the tips pass their nodes, and each stem ends in a flower. Then the greedy loop takes over:

on the right, each dashed circle is the largest free disc it found, just before a branch

grows to it. Big holes come first and slowly, small ones last and fast. The butterflies and

bees fly in, the bird glides onto its twig, and the snail crawls up its stem until the last

frame, which is exactly the page this seed always gives.

The growth is recorded once, while the page is laid out: each stem is also drawn as

prefixes of increasing length and each motif at a few smaller scales, replaying the same

random draws. A frame then writes the pieces whose time has come, in their original

painting order. make grow-6 renders one seed this way ( build/grow-6.gif and .mp4 , about

45 seconds); add EXPLAIN=1 for the dashed circles.

showcase.tex , "A year in the margin": spring on the first page, summer, autumn on the

last. Each section describes the feature it shows.

The grown margin can respond to the document around it:

Initials. \florilegiuminitial[5]{E} sets the first letter of a paragraph in a tile

five lines tall. The outline of the letter is read from an OpenType font (Latin Modern

Bold by default) and painted like a petal; a vine passes over and under its strokes in

turn, with leaves where they fit and flowers in the gaps, often in the letter's counters.

The letter is also typeset invisibly, so the paragraph still copies as "Every".

Flowers at the headings. With the option sections , every numbered section and

subsection gets a flower in the margin beside its heading, painted in the copper of the

accents, the way headings were once picked out in red.

A flower where the text asks. \florilegiumbloom puts a flower beside the line it

stands in; \florilegiumbloom[lily] asks for any motif of the garden. The marks are found

in the page box when the page is shipped out, so this works in one run.

Seasons. With the option aging , the garden ages from spring on the first page

(mostly in bud, small pale leaves) to autumn on the last (seed heads, falling petals, a

few copper leaves). It needs two runs, for the page count; \florilegiumage{0.8} sets an

One seed in spring, early summer, late summer and autumn. The seasons change what grows,

Most pages have visitors: a butterfly or two and bees in the open spaces, a snail crawling

up one of the main stems, and on about one page in five a bird perched on a twig of its own.

items.title: Infinite Mac: BeOS
items.summary: retrocomputing
items.content:
tl;dr: You can now run many BeOS versions in the browser at Infinite Mac , my site where you can experience the Macintosh Cinematic Universe from 1984 to 2005. The installs are full peers to their Mac cousins: you can boot them instantly (large disks are streamed in), play around with pre-installed software from Infinite HD, insert CD-ROMs from the Internet Archive, and save your work on the “Saved HD” drive.

BeOS was a multimedia-focused, multi-tasking and multi-threaded OS that was eventually ported to the Power Macintoshes of the mid-90s. It impressed many in the Mac community, including Apple itself, who considered acquiring Be, the company that had created it. If you’ve been following the saga of Apple’s search for a next-generation operating system, this lets you see what the road not taken was like.

After the last somewhat involved (though still satisfying) project on Infinite Mac, I was looking for a quicker win. BeOS had been on my radar for a while , and (unlike A/UX) I had a personal connection to it: I remember spotting a BeBox in Akihabara, making my Mac cosplay as it with BeView , and eventually dual-booting BeOS on my Power Macintosh 8500. DingusPPC, an emulator I had already integrated , was making good progress on running BeOS, so it seemed like adding it to the site would be mostly a matter of preparing some additional disk images.

Initially it appeared to be as straightforward as I had hoped; I added a Power Macintosh 7300 configuration (one of the Power Macs that was officially supported ), found an install CD , made a disk image , and was up and running . But as I used it more and started to install additional versions, I began to find a lot of small bugs and edge cases:

The BeOS boot loader thought that all modifier keys were being held down due to a bug in the ADB emulation ; this made it present the (ugly, PC BIOS-like) partition choice screen every time.

When changing the screen depth, there are two hardware components that need to be notified: the video controller and the digital-to-analog converter. DingusPPC had been accidentally relying on the order that Mac OS sent these notifications in; BeOS happened to make the opposite choice and would end up with a corrupted display.

Early versions of BeOS did video memory updates in little-endian mode 1 ; DingusPPC was missing support for that hardware capability.

Later versions of BeOS could mount HFS partitions, but they were having trouble with the volumes that I generated via the machfs Python library. It turned out that BeOS was (correctly) stricter than Mac OS about how some data structures should be populated.

And so on – most of the commits that I upstreamed to DingusPPC over the past month were in a quest for better BeOS compatibility.

SheepShaver , a Power Macintosh emulator that is still around today (and that Infinite Mac also embeds ), originated on BeOS. Mostly for the fun of another layer of inception/emulation, I wanted to make sure that it worked too. As it turned out, it also required a compatibility fix – it relied on an edge case of how the ROM is mapped to physical memory addresses that DingusPPC did not accurately model.

There is a pattern to most of these bug fixes: DingusPPC (and Infinite Mac) have been mostly focused on running Mac OS, and thus accidentally became dependent on its quirks or implementation choices. Adding an independently developed operating system to the mix exercised new paths, and ended up improving the accuracy of the emulated hardware. To be clear, DingusPPC was pretty close out of the box; kudos to its maintainers . I believe that, with this work, it’s the only emulator 2 that can run PowerPC versions of BeOS. I’m also hopeful that this will help with bringing up alternate operating systems like MkLinux (which I also have memories of) and Rhapsody .

On the Infinite Mac side, there were obvious changes like a “BeOS” appearance for my custom controls and collecting software for the library. I also…

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: The AI-Energy-Fascism Nexus
items.content:
Too often, our tech criticism gets stuck in a form of analysis we might describe as the assholes critique .

Here, strategy and organising get sidelined in favour of gawking at the ideological freak show. We might start by asking: why are there so many damn data centres popping up right now? How do we stop the worst such projects from taking root in our communities? But this easily morphs into a different set of questions: Who in their right mind would need to build this much compute? Have you heard about these tech billionaires’ odd views on AI surpassing humans, about their enthusiasm for eugenic arbitrage, or their bizarre beliefs about the Anti-Christ? 1 Thereafter — in group chats, on online platforms, in organising calls — things devolve into swapping links about TESCREAL philosophies, Elon Musk’s assorted perversities, and the remarkable stupidity of singularity bros. 2

The assholes critique is certainly compelling. The worldviews gathering force amongst the billionaire classes are obviously important factors shaping the worlds we all share. There is real value in understanding why our enemies think the way they do, what their influences are, and the focal points of their desires. There are also surely libidinal satisfactions to be had in uncovering these at-times-cryptic motivations.

There are, however, limits to this approach. For one, it focuses a bit too much on individuals and ideas, jumping over the ways that even billionaires need to build coalitions across differences and manage conflicting goals in order to act on the world outside their homes. Typically, this involves the boards of publicly traded companies, the matryoshkas of political jurisdictions and regulators, and a public that at least nominally must be convinced not to follow through on those jokey guillotine memes.

Knowing what an individual believes doesn’t tell us much about what they can do . This is the key difference between biography and strategy. This is of particular importance when trying to account for the irrational exuberance of market actors engaging in what is almost certainly a destructive economic bubble. 3 While a deep-pocketed individual might be able to gamble their ill-gotten wealth on profoundly under-elaborated bids to build a robot god, this is a lot harder for corporate board members, who have a fiduciary responsibility to maximise value for shareholders (at least from quarter to quarter). If they piss away Microsoft or Amazon’s stock value, shareholders can and will sue them to hell and back. Regulators, too, may well step in to prevent them from crashing the whole economy (at least election cycle to election cycle). What’s more, tech billionaires explicitly require the state to coordinate the conditions that allow them to keep importing and installing GPUs, sucking up more and more energy on increasingly unstable grids; and to continue to appropriate lands from a variety of political constituencies and biomes, in order to build their giant concrete server farms.

What the tech-freak CEO thus needs is less conviction in his own beliefs than a bridge between them and those of his allies. He needs to propose a bargain in which enough powerful interests see at least a temporary reason to join in the pursuit of AGI and data centre expansion. This is a tall order: the AGI project is obviously foolish, and the bubble is doomed to end badly. 4 But perhaps there are just enough reasons for just enough partners in industry and government to form a coalition with this tech idiot, at least for part of the way.

Understanding these aligned rationales helps us better understand our enemies as they cohere across divergent goals and worldviews, all nonetheless opposed to left imaginings of the future. Many of them are indeed assholes, but their efficacy comes less from certainty in their own rotten accounts of social life than from their ability to build alliances and wield power.

items.content:

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 보기에는 블랙해커들 보다는 서버측이 클라이언트의 행동을 분석하는 과정처럼 보이더군요..

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-109231 📢 Source: Wordfence 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Access of Private Data via Activation Token Reuse in versions up to, and including, 4.1.4. This is due to the `on_user_email_changed` hook — which is responsible for rotating the activation token and recording a pending-email-change marker on an unactivated Customer account — only being registered inside the `is_double_opt_in_login_enabled()` branch when "Disable login for unactivated customers" is set to Yes, leaving the original `?activate=` token valid and entirely unbound to the email address it was issued for when that setting is No. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to change their account email to a victim's billing email via the standard `/my-account/edit-account/` form and then redeem their original activation token through `customer_account_activate()`, triggering `link_customer_past_orders()` to reassign any matching guest order to the attacker's account and exposing the original buyer's billing name, street address, phone number, and purchased items on the attacker's My Account order page. Exploitation requires the site to have double opt-in enabled with "Disable login for unactivated customers" explicitly set to No (a non-default configuration), public customer registration enabled, and the original activation token redeemed within its one-day expiry window. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-31T09:29:27.848Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-109231

items.content_ko: 이 취약점의 원인은 on_user_email_changed 훅이 '비활성 고객 로그인 차단' 설정이 Yes일 때만 등록되는 데 있다. 설정이 No이면 이메일 변경 시 활성화 토큰이 갱신되거나 이메일과 묶이지 않아, 원래 ?activate= 토큰이 계속 유효하다. 공격자는 /my-account/edit-account/ 양식으로 계정 이메일을 피해자의 청구 이메일로 바꾼 뒤, 원래 활성화 토큰을 customer_account_activate()로 사용한다. 그러면 link_customer_past_orders()가 일치하는 게스트 주문을 공격자 계정에 재할당해, 원 구매자의 청구 이름, 거리 주소, 전화번호, 구매 내역 일부가 노출된다. 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 나머지 내용은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Breaking the open web won't stop the bad bots
items.content:
A close up of a spider in its web. Valeriia Neganova/ Unsplash

Late last month , more than 300 representatives from major media outlets were on Capitol Hill to advocate for the Stealth Bot Prohibition Act . They came with a legitimate grievance. Newsrooms are being hit by a surge of automated traffic, mostly from AI developers. AI developers extract enormous volumes of online content and then potentially deprive website owners of referral traffic and ad revenue with generative AI features and chatbots trained on that content. It is a real problem that deserves a real solution. But this bill doesn’t directly target the harms caused by abusive crawling. Instead, it would force anyone accessing a website automatically to identify themselves and their purposes for collecting public information. Rather than protect journalists, the bill threatens a basic tool they, and many others, rely on to gather information online.

Cutting-edge investigative journalism relies on automated data collection. In 2022, a Pulitzer-winning Wall Street Journal investigation analyzed over 31,000 financial disclosures from 12,000 senior government employees, revealing that nearly a quarter of federal officials traded stock in industries their agencies regulated. To conduct an investigation at that scale, the Journal relied on web scraping: an automated process where a software bot, known as a crawler, browses the internet and collects information. This fundamental tool of the open web is now under threat from bills that purport to target “stealth crawling,” but in reality would hamper legitimate public-interest activities, including preservation, journalism, research, and security.

Again, aggressive, large-scale scraping is a real problem — particularly as demand for AI training and content has exploded. It can overwhelm websites, increase costs, and threaten institutions that produce and preserve knowledge, including commercial publishers, Wikipedia , libraries , and the Internet Archive , where one of the authors of this piece works.

In an apparent attempt to reduce or eliminate problematic scraping practices, proposed bills, like the federal Stealth Bot Prohibition Act and New York’s Stealth Crawler Prohibition Act, would impose sweeping prohibitions on anonymous scraping without addressing the real harms.

Both bills define a “bot” or “crawler” as software that “retrieves, scans, indexes, scrapes, or otherwise accesses a website or other internet source.” A bot is “stealth” if it fails to disclose its identity and the “specific nature and purpose of the bot.” Under the federal bill, the FTC can pursue penalties of up to $53,000 if a person uses a stealth bot in a way that is “reasonably likely to damage, impair, or burden” a website’s “technical or commercial operation.” The bill provides no definition or standard of what is reasonably likely to impair a website. Under the New York bill, which only applies to covered news sites, a publisher can obtain a subpoena to unmask a crawler’s identity without requiring a showing of any harm.

Knowing the identity behind a crawler tells us relatively little about whether its behavior is harmful. Under the New York bill, a company that discloses its identity and then accesses the website 10,000 times a minute complies with the law even though it is still imposing enormous and likely unjustified costs on the site. But a journalist anonymously using a crawler to investigate potentially anti-competitive practices by tech companies does not. Many of the most socially valuable uses of crawling require anonymity. Revealing a crawler’s identity and purposes can change the very nature of the information that is collected; if the subject of the study knows it is being observed and by whom, its behavior will change. That is the point of studying it anonymously.

Moreover, not all automated data collection is abusive, and not all of it is used to train AI, but these proposed bills risk deterring archivists,…

items.title: How curl was accidentally Turing-complete for nine months
items.summary: compsci
items.content:
From curl 8.12 through 8.16, config files could slice variable values and include other config files without an explicit depth cap. Together, these features let curl simulate any two-counter Minsky program. Under the usual idealization of unbounded strings and resources, this construction was Turing-complete.

Curl 8.17.0 added a five-level include cap that breaks this reduction.

A counter value n is represented by n copies of x .

Each instruction state uses one or more config files, with file names acting as labels, and expand-config selecting the next file.

With that, we can compile any two-counter program into curl config files.

Four files in curl_addition.zip compute 2 + 3.

The reduction assumes unbounded counters and unbounded steps. The real binary has neither:

The pull request says the cap prevents a config file from including itself indefinitely. Its regression test does exactly that and expects an error. The public explanation does not discuss Turing completeness or why the cap is five.

A Bash while loop can complement bounded curl by invoking a config once per step and carrying the counters and instruction label between invocations. The repetition then comes from Bash, so this is a composition rather than curl-alone Turing completeness.
items.title_ko: curl이 9개월 동안 우발적으로 튜링 완전(Turing-complete)했던 과정
items.summary_ko: curl 8.12부터 8.16까지는 설정 파일이 변수 값을 자르고 다른 설정 파일을 포함할 수 있었으며, 포함 깊이에 명시적 제한이 없었다. 이 기능들로 두 개의 카운터를 가진 Minsky 프로그램을 흉내 낼 수 있었고, 문자열과 자원이 무제한이라는 가정 아래 튜링 완전했다. curl 8.17.0이 포함(include)을 다섯 단계로 제한하면서 이 구성은 깨졌다.
items.content_ko: 카운터 값 n은 x의 n개 복사본으로 표현되며, 각 명령 상태는 파일 이름을 레이블로 삼는 하나 이상의 설정 파일로 구현된다. 이 방식으로 두 카운터 프로그램을 curl 설정 파일로 컴파일할 수 있다. 예시로 2 + 3을 계산하는 파일 네 개가 제공된다. 다만 이 환원은 무제한 카운터와 무제한 단계를 가정하며, 실제 바이너리에는 그런 자원이 없다. Pull request는 설정 파일이 자기 자신을 무한정 포함하는 것을 막기 위한 제한이라고 설명하며, 회귀 테스트도 그 경우에 오류가 나는지를 확인한다. 공개된 설명에는 튜링 완전성이나 다섯 단계라는 기준의 이유가 언급되지 않았다.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

items.title: Proton’s CEO Cancels AI ‘Re-Interviews’
items.content:
On Friday, Andy Yen, the CEO of Proton, cancelled a series of nearly company-wide ‘re-interviews’ that would have forced employees to explain how they are using AI, with the clear intention that they may be fired if not using it enough in the eyes of Proton leadership, according to six current Proton employees and audio of an around two hour all-hands meeting obtained by 404 Media.

The move came after 404 Media published an investigation on Thursday, which showed how Yen was aggressively pushing AI across Proton, in some cases despite security concerns from employees. In one exchange, an employee in the company’s security Slack channel urged Proton to at least take a few days to pentest newly written code before pushing it live. “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure,” Yen wrote in the channel at the end of August. “Stop thinking always of how to be slower, and focus more on how to be faster.” Yen added, “stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more.”

The re-interview cancellations likely don’t address the concerns of many Proton users, who are more focused on Proton’s deprioritization of security; many Proton users have blasted the company’s leadership on social media over the last 24 hours and explicitly called for Yen to resign.

It painted a picture of Proton that is very different to the public’s perception of a company carefully protecting privacy. Instead, Proton is barreling ahead with AI in large part to achieve more annual revenue. The investigation also found a culture of fear across Proton, where employees have genuine concerns about security or being asked to develop security-focused products with AI, but feel unable to voice them because Yen mocks or insults employees in front of everyone else.

“I don’t think he will change anything, and I think the only reason we had this meeting is because he has a rebellion on his hands,” one employee told 404 Media after the all-hands meeting on Friday.

Near the start of the meeting, Yen said, “I want to acknowledge myself, personally, that there was a communication failure on my part and there are many things that probably could and should have been communicated differently, and this is something that I’ll have to reflect on and improve over time. So I will do that.”

“So what does that mean going forward? Going forward, I'm still going to push,” he added.

Yen said leadership gathered in the last couple of days to talk about the re-interviews, and spoke to the Proton board too. “They’re closely monitoring the situation,” Yen said. (Proton is owned by the Proton Foundation, whose board of trustees includes Yen, Sir Tim Berners Lee, Prof. Carissa Veliz, Dingchao Lu, and Antonio Gambardella.)

Yen also mentioned “org changes,” and said that part of this is “redistributing talent across teams.” He said that the reorganization will happen next month, “but there will be no loss of jobs from AI.”

Later in the call, Butler said Yen “needs to, and he has committed to, doing better” regarding how he communicates with his employees. “Using AI effectively and pragmatically does not mean that we’ve given up on security, or good architecture, or sound software engineering principles,” he added.

items.title: Show HN: A working Nintendo in ~1GB of Qwen weights
items.content:
An NES CPU compiled into the weights of a stock Qwen3.5 model.

The NES's 6502 CPU (the core of its 2A03 chip), its 2 KB of work RAM, and a cartridge's program

ROM run inside a standard Qwen3_5ForCausalLM checkpoint. Nobody trained these weights; a

compiler computed every one. When you play a game, the model predicts the CPU's execution log

one token at a time. A small host program plays the rest of the console around it: it draws the

picture, reads the controller, and fires the vblank interrupt.

nesformer builds on Qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal , which

compiled a CHIP-8 and then a RISC-V CPU into Qwen3.5-4B. It reuses Qwenputer's compiler and its

central trick: the model's Gated DeltaNet state is the machine's memory.

Full Game by Doug Fraker (title screen and first level)

Every CPU token in these runs came from the model. For the bundled test games, every frame also

matches a conventional 6502 emulator's output exactly (see How it was checked ).

Unzip nesformer.zip and nesformer-weights.zip into the same folder. The weights go next to

├── roms/ <- test ROMs (put your own here too)

├── examples/ <- sample GIFs and frame sheets

└── weights/ <- from nesformer-weights.zip

The CLI looks for weights/ beside the nesformer/ package. To keep the weights elsewhere,

--show draws each frame in your terminal as the model generates it. When the run ends, the CLI

saves an animated GIF named after the ROM (here thwaite.gif ) in the current folder.

Expect it to be slow. The first run spends about 20 seconds compiling the engine with numba.

After that, a frame takes 1–6 seconds, so 600 frames (10 seconds of NES time) take around

items.summary_ko: 닌텐도 NES의 6502 CPU, 작업용 RAM, 카트리지 프로그램 ROM이 표준 Qwen3.5 모델의 가중치 안에서 실행되도록 컴파일된 프로젝트다. 가중치는 학습된 것이 아니라 컴파일러가 계산해 만들었으며, 게임을 실행하면 모델이 CPU 실행 로그를 토큰 단위로 예측한다. 기존 6502 에뮬레이터와 프레임 출력이 정확히 일치하는 것으로 확인되었다고 한다.
items.content_ko: NES의 6502 CPU(2A03 칩의 핵심), 2KB 작업 RAM, 카트리지의 프로그램 ROM이 표준 Qwen3_5ForCausalLM 체크포인트 안에서 실행된다. 이 가중치는 누군가 학습시킨 것이 아니라 컴파일러가 하나하나 계산해 만들었다. 게임을 플레이하면 모델이 CPU 실행 로그를 한 번에 한 토큰씩 예측하고, 호스트 프로그램이 화면 출력, 컨트롤러 입력 처리, vblank 인터럽트 발생 등 나머지 콘솔 기능을 담당한다. nesformer는 Divyansh Agrawal의 Qwenputer를 기반으로 만들어졌다. Qwenputer는 CHIP-8과 RISC-V CPU를 Qwen3.5-4B에 컴파일한 프로젝트이며, nesformer는 그 컴파일러와 핵심 아이디어인 Gated DeltaNet 상태가 기계의 메모리 역할을 한다는 방식을 재사용한다. 번들된 테스트 게임에서는 실행 중 CPU 토큰이 모두 모델에서 나왔고, 모든 프레임이 기존 6502 에뮬레이터의 출력과 정확히 일치했다. 설치하려면 nesformer.zip과 nesformer-weights.zip을 같은 폴더에 압축 해제하고, 테스트용 ROM은 roms 폴더에 넣으면 된다.

items.title: If you love a website, back it up
items.summary: web
items.content:
This story starts with a little tragedy. See, I’ve got these old webpages I love to go back and look on every now and then. There’s websites that have been online unchanged for years and years, or decades, and there’s something a little cozy about checking in on them every now and then to see an old friend is still doing okay. Sometimes, of course, tragedy strikes.

There was this fansite called teapuppies.com for an old anime series and and toy line called Ochaken . It’s about these cute cartoon dog characters who have tea leaves for ears, each of them named after a different kind of tea. 1 The site had been online since 2004 and had basically not changed since 2005, but it was nice just having it around. Except when I went to visit it a few weeks ago, and discovered that not only was the site gone but the domain is now being used to serve online gambling ads.

I work in web archiving, by the way. Which is to say that I should have known the site would go offline someday, and that I have the tools to have done something about it. I could have archived that site while it was still around, but I didn’t. This post is here to beg you to do what I didn’t think to, and to teach you how.

You see, when I talk to a lot of people about web archiving, they always seem to believe it’s something they couldn’t do. It’s something a big organization like the Internet Archive does, and if you want a webpage to be saved you just have to wait and hope it gets done. But that’s not true! What I really want everyone to know is that you have control over the world around you, you can take action to preserve things and make things better. And not just can , but should ! Don’t just wait for someone else to act - get out there and and make it happen! Got a favourite site? Back it up! Got some information you don’t want to get lost? Back it up! Favourite post somewhere? All together now. Back! It! Up!

All of the tools I’ll be showing off in this post use standard web archiving formats like WARC 2 . You don’t have to worry about any of the technical details 3 , but I’m telling you that because it means there are a lot of really great tools to do whatever you want with them. Here, just as an example, is an entire archived website embedded right in this blog post:

You can even click through all the links, look at all of the images, the works. It’s an entire website right in a post! (And if you don’t trust me to keep this up, and you want the web archive to host somewhere else? You can download it for yourself right from there. Just click the kebab menu and choose “download archive”, and you can do whatever you like with it. In fact, please do!)

By the way, for disclosure: the tools I’m going to mention in this blog post are made by the company I work for, but that’s not because they’ll pay my salary (most of them are free!). I just happen to think these are the best tools there are for personal web archiving.

Option 1 - ArchiveWeb.page browser extension

By far the easiest personal web archiving tool is the ArchiveWeb.page browser extension for Chrome. This doesn’t take much in the way of setup or technical skills, and it works for anything: a single page, an entire website, a social media post or profile. So long as you can see it in a web browser, you can save it. All you really need to do is:

Visit the first page you want to archive.

Click the ArchiveWeb.page icon in the toolbar, then click “Start Archiving”.

If your page has any interactive elements, click on those to make sure all their data loads.

Visit any other pages you want captured in the same collection and let the extension grab them.

Click the ArchiveWeb.page icon in the toolbar, then click “Stop Archiving”.

You’re done! You just archived a web page! Now that it’s all saved, you can preview it and see how it went by clicking the extension’s icon and then the home icon to open the extension dashboard. From there, you can click on your archiving session to preview the pages you…

items.content_ko: 필자는 오랫동안 바뀌지 않은 옛 웹페이지를 종종 찾아보곤 했다. 그중 Ochaken 팬사이트 teapuppies.com은 2004년부터 온라인에 있었고 2005년 이후로는 거의 변하지 않았다. 몇 주 전 방문했을 때 사이트는 사라져 있었고, 도메인은 온라인 도박 광고에 쓰이고 있었다. 필자는 웹 아카이빙을 하는 사람으로서 사이트가 언젠가 사라질 수 있다는 것을 알았고, 아카이브할 도구도 있었지만 그렇게 하지 않았다고 고백한다. 이 글은 독자들에게 그렇게 하지 않은 일을 미리 해 두도록 권하며, 그 방법을 설명하기 위해 쓰였다.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: Sam Altman Absolutely Hates the Idea of People Running Their Own AI Models at Home, Argues They Shouldn’t Own Computers: He'd prefer if we surrender all our RAM to data centers.
items.content:
Shares of US chipmaker Intel cratered on Friday, plunging almost 30 percent, the worst stock collapse in 52 years . The wipeout, analysts said, could be due to a massive slowdown in the PC market . The market softness shouldn’t come to anybody’s surprise, given the AI boom has made individual components, most notably memory and storage, practically unaffordable.

However, leaders of AI frontier labs aren’t blinking. To OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, for instance, having people run their own models at home on their own computers doesn’t make any sense anyway. During a recent interview on the Cheeky Pint podcast , Altman argued that ongoing memory supply chain woes were because selfish individuals wanted to run their AI models locally instead of leaving the remaining AI chips alone for hyperscalers to hoard in data centers.

“A lot of people want local inference,” he said. “And somehow, they assume, that the problem is solved now. Because we are going to have open-source models. We’re going to be able to run them on our own computers. And so we’re not going to need all the stuff in the data center.”

“But from a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of [dynamic RAM] sitting in their own computer,” he added.

Instead of running their own models at home, a trend that has blown up thanks to the emergence of open-weight models from China , Altman argued that the cloud — run by hyperscalers like OpenAI — is the answer.

“You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very constrained environment,” he said. “And somehow everyone’s, many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”

It’s a particularly tone-deaf argument that throws fuel on the fire of tech enthusiasts everywhere, who have watched as individual components have skyrocketed in price . Just earlier this month, Altman argued that the “world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology,” which similarly drew a heated response.

Altman’s latest comments drew the ire of the PC gaming community.

“What a self-centered POS,” one enraged Reddit user wrote . “Cult leader mentality really shining with this one.”

“He seems to not be able to comprehend the idea of people wanting to own their own computers,” another wrote . “Like it’s an alien concept to him.”

“Privately owned companies with the sole interest of profit should not be making monumental decisions that affect the vast majority of the population,” one user argued . “But maybe I’m the crazy one.”

The news comes as the AI industry continues to struggle to commercialize their offerings. It’s a particularly hairy situation as their expenses are still ballooning at alarming rates, terrifying investors.

The concept of running local inference on their own machines undermines the very concept of relying exclusively on expensive cloud services being offered by the likes of OpenAI. In other words, it’s no wonder Altman hates the idea of people owning their own machines.

His latest comments also speak to frontier AI labs desperately trying to secure AI chips as available supplies run low. There’s a massive circuit board shortage as PC makers say they’re already fully booked through the end of 2030 .

But to Altman, cutting out individual owners of computers capable of running AI models isn’t a problem. After all, as he argued during the latest podcast appearance, the cloud is a far better use of available hardware.

“Given that the world is going to be limited in its silicon capacity, we all have a shared interest,” he said.

Infuriated tech enthusiasts, however, are likely to disagree with that sentiment.

items.title: 사생활침해 범죄가 의심 됩니다. 도움이 필요합니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-107711 📢 Source: Wordfence 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False The FlexStock – Product Stock Sync with Google Sheets for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'products[].post_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.17.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable by any Subscriber-level user because the plugin's admin_enqueue_scripts callback exposes the REST bearer token in the Dashboard page source via wp_localize_script() without a capability check, and the REST endpoint's permission_callback validates only that bearer token rather than performing a current_user_can() capability check. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-31T09:29:27.498Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-107711
items.title_ko: FlexStock 플러그인, 저장형 XSS 취약점(CVE-2026-107711)
items.summary_ko: WordPress 플러그인 FlexStock – Product Stock Sync with Google Sheets for WooCommerce 3.17.2 이하 버전에 'products[].post_content' 매개변수 입력 검증 부족으로 저장형 XSS 취약점이 있다고 Wordfence가 보고했다. 구독자 이상 권한의 인증된 공격자가 악성 스크립트를 주입해, 해당 페이지에 접속하는 사용자에게서 스크립트가 실행될 수 있다. 관리자 대시보드에서 REST 베어러 토큰이 노출되고, REST 엔드포인트가 권한 검사 없이 토큰만 확인하는 것이 악용 조건으로 설명되어 있다.
items.content_ko: 플러그인의 admin_enqueue_scripts 콜백이 wp_localize_script()를 통해 REST 베어러 토큰을 대시보드 페이지 소스에 권한 검사 없이 노출한다. 또한 REST 엔드포인트의 permission_callback은 current_user_can() 권한 검사 대신 베어러 토큰만 확인한다. 이 때문에 구독자 수준 사용자도 공격에 악용할 수 있다고 원문은 설명한다. 공격자는 'products[].post_content' 매개변수에 악성 스크립트를 주입할 수 있으며, 주입된 페이지에 접속하는 사용자에게서 스크립트가 실행된다. 게시일은 2026-10-31이다.
